title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber
summary: Uber engineers describe the model gateway, MCP gateway, agent sandboxes, skills marketplace and context graph behind their agent-built software pipeline.

assertions.quote: more than 70% of our PRs now either by local or cloud agents.

verdicts.note: Google and Microsoft executives cite ~25-50% of new code AI-generated; the figures are self-reported and usually count accepted suggestions, not finished code.
Citing company disclosures: Google and Microsoft said in 2025 that AI writes over 20% of their new code. This is secondhand and a meaningful but not majority share.
Cites public statements from Microsoft, Meta and Google that roughly a third of their new code is AI-generated; secondhand.

Google reports that AI completion assisted 67% of code characters (38% acceptance rate), so more characters are AI-completed than typed by hand; note this is a completion metric, not autonomous authorship.

assertions.quote: We handled more than 250 automated migrations 9 million lines of code automatically for our engineers.

verdicts.note: Migration case studies (Google, Amazon Java upgrades, Airbnb) got their scale from pairing LLMs with deterministic tooling and validation rather than free-form generation.

assertions.quote: we projected all of these MCPS into CLI pattern so that even the response doesn't eat up in your context.

verdicts.note: Each MCP server injects tool schemas into context; large servers can use tens of thousands of tokens, and agents use CLIs well. Deferred tool loading has since reduced this.

assertions.quote: with and without graph we see massive improvement in tokens, turns and latency

verdicts.note: Relevant org context plausibly cuts rework, but the cited 50% token / one-shot result is a single vendor test, not independent evidence.

assertions.quote: So what we built an entire life cycle around skills.

verdicts.note: Reusable commands/skills reduce variance and share practice across a team; the 'three times' threshold is a rule of thumb.

assertions.quote: to build more advanced like endtoend features we really need to be able to validate uh the feature first

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: we can probably build it now it's more of a question of should we build it

verdicts.note: Consistent with Amdahl-style reasoning and reports of shifting PM:engineer ratios; evidence is mostly anecdotal from AI-native teams.

assertions.quote: the roles of engineers are getting blurred.

verdicts.note: Role blurring is widely reported anecdotally, but there is no solid labor-market evidence yet that specialists are losing ground.
Anthropic: engineers report becoming 'more full-stack' (backend engineers building UIs, researchers building front-end visualizations), but nothing shows value moving away from specialists.
